free_tier.stated: Jules free plan: 15 daily tasks on a rolling 24-hour window, 3 concurrent tasks, Gemini 2.5 Pro, quoted: "Daily Tasks (rolling 24 hours) | 15", "Concurrent Tasks | 3", "Model Access | Gemini 2.5 Pro"

interface_detail: the Jules Tools CLI and the web app; the REST endpoints the CLI calls are undocumented; not probed
tooling: the Jules web app at jules.google.com and the Jules Tools CLI (npm package @google/jules); the CLI also exports settings, environment variables, scheduled tasks, memories and every session to a local folder
chaining: each task runs in a fresh virtual machine that clones a connected GitHub repository, so each free daily task is a short-lived build and test machine; dev servers and watch scripts are not supported in setup scripts, and the route stops taking new work after November 11, 2026

limits.value: a rolling 24-hour window of 15 tasks stops new work first; the product disables the New task button and waits for the window to roll.

identity_cost.detail: a Google account: the getting-started guide says to sign in with a Google account, accept a one-time privacy notice and connect a GitHub account to the repositories Jules works on; paid plans need a Google AI subscription on an individual @gmail.com account. The guide describes no card or phone step for the free plan.

notes: A coding subscription: Jules is a coding agent with a free plan, and higher task limits come with the Google AI Pro and Ultra plans. No coding-subs record holds it, and none is proposed because the product is winding down (see reliability_note); the vendor points users to Google Antigravity, recorded at coding-subs/antigravity. It sits in compute because each task runs in its own virtual machine. The free tier is capped by tasks, not by tokens or minutes, and the page states no per-task wall clock. The free plan gets Gemini 2.5 Pro while the paid plans start with Gemini 3 Pro. The age requirement is 18 or older.
